utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please kindly call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. I would like to welcome all the people present in the courtroom, the representatives of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused and all the other people assisting us in the courtroom today. We are Thursday, the 10th of January, 2008. Mr. Pusic is still ill, I believe. Mr. Petkovic will join us a bit later, and I think we can start. Mr. Karnavas, I think you would like to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours. Perhaps we can go into closed session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Closed session, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Or private session. I get those two confused. It is with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: I will read the summary of the statement of the benefit of the public. The witness, a former Territorial Defence member lived with his family from August 1992 until his detention in Novi Seher. Witness EI described the attack of the HVO on Nova Seher on 26th June, 1993, and the surrender of the witness and the civilian population on 29 June 1993. They were all taken to Zepce where the military-aged men were separated from the rest. The HVO detained about 450 men in the sports hall at Perkovic and beat some of them. After seven days on that prison were transported by JNA buses, driven by Serb soldiers to Bosansko Grahova. The guards on the buses were, however, HVO, and at a check-point all the Serb military were replaced by HVO military and the detainees were taken further to Vitina and put in a hangar there in the Ljubuski municipality. The witness was detained at Vitina camp for two months, and saw Hamdija Tabakovic severely beaten by HVO soldiers. He describes the facility and the overcrowded conditions. Initially the HVO military police guarded them, and then the home guards took over. They were taken to do forced labour at the front lines in Gola Brda, Vrde, and other places. In one of those locations, Witness EI saw HV personnel and tanks. During forced labour, HVO soldiers threatened detainee's with death, insulted, and mistreated them, in some cases resulting in injuries, including gun-shot wounds. At Vrde, 20 detainees were once used, as the witness says human shields and to perform military tasks. After the HVO wounded the witness in his feet, he was transferred to the Heliodrom where he was treated and registered by the ICRC in December 1993. Although the ICRC also visited Vrde, the HVO did not allow them to register the detainees there. The detainees at Heliodrom were also taken by the HVO for forced labour on the front lines in Mostar. Many detainees were wounded and one Bosnian Muslim of those witnesses that he knew, Ibrahim Jasic, died of his wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness EI. Witness, could you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: I will refer to you as Witness EI because you have some protective measures rendered by the Trial Chamber, as you understand. I will ask you some questions related to your statement. Did you provide a written statement to the investigators of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you remember when you gave that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Was it on the 16th March 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And at the time you provided the written statement, did you answer the questions to the investigator truthfully?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And did you answer those questions as well freely without any coercion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And at the end of the interview, the statement was read back to you in the -- in B/C/S, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And then you write -- you signed -- you initialised and signed that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And in Kopice in February 2007, you confirmed the contents of that statement to an officer from the registry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you. And at that time you have a B/C/S copy of that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And you were allowed to make any corrections and modifications?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And you agreed with the statement as it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: I will ask now the usher to assist us to give a copy of the exhibit -- Prosecution Exhibit 10210. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So, Witness, can you see your statement now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And do you recognise the signature as yours in that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And do you have any additions to make to that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And do you have to make any corrections to that statement today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And if I were to ask you questions about the subject matters contained in that statement, would your answers reflect whatever is written in that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: I would tender into evidence that statement, Your Honour, under seal according to the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So you heard the Trial Chamber, we have to concentrate on the events that took place in Vitina, so I will ask you questions related to that. In paragraph 10 of your statement you mentioned that 450 Bosnian Muslims were transferred to Vitina camp. Could you describe the group? Were they were civilians or only military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both the military and the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And you mentioned in paragraph 10 that immediately when you arrived into Vitina some soldiers looked for Hamdija Tabakovic. What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when they found him there they started hitting him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And do you know what happened with Mr. Tabakovic afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Did he stay there in Vitina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they took him away the first night, and I never -- I've never heard anything about him anymore. I heard that he got killed, that they killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now in relation to the living conditions in Vitina, what was the food you have there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, those who didn't go to work, they got a quarter of a loaf of bread, and those who did go to work would get a hot meal and a quarter of a loaf of bread [Realtime transcript read in error "some bread and a quarter of meal"].

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And did you have a doctor there for the 450 detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And what about water? Did you have water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was some rain-water.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So basically if it would not rain, would you have water there?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to intervene. It appears to me that the record is wrong. At page 90 line 8 as far as I could understand the witness in his language he said that if they went to work they could eat a hot meal and a loaf -- and some bread and it says here that they could get a quarter of a meal. So if we could have that corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So you were referring to the fact that you were having only water from rain-water. What happened when it was not raining there, did you have access to water if the water was finished?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was a well, a water well there -- well, maybe they brought some water there in water tank trucks, but there was some water there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And were you allowed to have a shower for the prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: How many times you were allowed to have a shower?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Once a week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you mentioned that in the beginning the HVO military police guarded Vitina hangar. How were they dressed, those members of the HVO military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in camouflage clothes, and they had belts and pistols.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And what colour was that belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: White.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And then you mentioned that the HVO military police was replaced.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: By whom was it replaced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The home guard. That's what they were called.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are now going to concentrate on the incidents of forced labour that you mentioned, some of them. You said that you were sent to Gola Brda, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And in your statement you mentioned that in Gola Brda you saw members of the Croatian military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what a soldier told us, that he was from Dubrovnik, that he was a Croatian army soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And after two months in Vitina and going to Gola Brda and to other areas, you were sent to Vrde, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vrde.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Right. And what did you have to do there at Vrde?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we dug trenches. We did some engineering work at the line. We built bunkers, and we brought food to the soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And who transported you from Vitina hangar to Vrde?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were brought there by truck. We boarded the truck and we were brought to Vrde.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And just before we discuss the subject of Vrde. When you were in the Vitina hangar you said that you were 450 detainees. Could you please describe the condition of that hangar, how big it was -- it was sufficient for all the 450 detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the hangar was 15 by 10 in size. The conditions there were not good. There were just wooden boards down there and that was all, and in front of the hangar there were some 50 men because we couldn't all fit in. So 50 people, 50 of us, were there in front of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And when you had to sleep, where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, right there where we were. I was in the hangar but some 50 people were outside the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Did you sleep on the floor, on the couch, there was a bed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the wooden boards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: In relation to Vrde, what soldiers brought you to Vrde?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see the insignia, but they were HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you remember from what unit they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And where were you lodged there in Vrde?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were in a house. Half of the house was where we lived and the other half was where a well, a water well, was, that's where we took the water out to drink and to wash.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Did you have any beds there to sleep or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: I want you to concentrate on the incident when you were wounded on your foot. Could you please briefly describe what happened that day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were on the line. Ten people escaped on that day and we were all gathered together down there, and they were looking for Meho to call on the ten people who had fled to come back. They took him away and these men did not come back. Then he brought us down there to the house where we were sleeping. He took five men up there, and after a short while Salko Deronja came back, he was wounded in the leg, and then I was taken away. I went up there and I saw the people, they had been beaten up, they were all swollen, I could hardly recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And did anyone take care of your wound at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So could you describe after the -- after they took you to the -- they call you back, what happened to you at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when I arrived at the headquarters, I was told that I was not supposed to answer nothing or I don't know. They asked me who had organized the escape and I said I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Now, what happened to you after you answered that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander then pulled his pistol, put it in my mouth, against my neck and into my ear, and he said that he would shoot me if I didn't say. I said I didn't know. And then he grabbed my foot and he shot me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Was anyone else wounded on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Salko was shot before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And after they shot at you on your foot, did they take care of that wound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they took me to a place where there was a doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And that was immediately after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, after five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that after the -- before the wounds you were used as a human shield in Vrde?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: What do you mean you were used as a human shield? Could you please briefly describe that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was this fighting around the Relej or the relay station which was held by the HVO. The BH army attacked that area and they took a part of it, and we were told that we were supposed to take some ammunition and grenades up there. 20 of our prisoners went there and also some soldiers, and that's how we went up there to the Relej.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You mentioned that you were registered by the ICRC at one point. Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was at Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And how many times have you been visited by the ICRC at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three or four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And have you been visited in another place or have you seen the ICRC in another place before being registered in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: With the assistance of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I will ask to show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P 10211.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Witness EI, do you recognise the certificate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: When did you get that certificate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got it when I was released from the camp, and that was after the new year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And do you agree with the dates recorded in the certificate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Could you please explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 2nd of January here, 1993, I wasn't in the camp at that time, it was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So just to point out to Your Honours because it looks like it was a typo, a mistake in that certificate and it's missing the number 1 of December, 12 December. Thank you very much. I have no more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. There may be 30 minutes left. Who is the counsel who wants to carry out his or her cross-examination? Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It is the turn of General Petkovic's Defence to start off with the cross-examination, that is why I am taking the floor first. I'm going to ask you a few very simple questions, Witness, just to clarify certain details but before that could you clear something up. In January 1999, did you give a statement to the agency for research and documentation in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well I did give a statement, yes. I don't know whether that's the one you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, if the usher could help us out we could show you the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the statement ready here, copies for the Trial Chamber and everybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm just going to compare that statement of yours with the statement you gave to the ICTY Prosecutor to try and clarify some details. In the statement you gave to the Prosecution of this Tribunal you said that for two months you were in Vitina, and in the statement that you gave to the research and documentation agency you say that you were there for one month and that after one month you left and went to the village of Vrde. Now, can you explain that to us. How long were you in Vitina for, in fact, one month or two months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About two months.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: About two months, right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, if you handed yourself over on the 29th of June and if seven days later you arrived in Vitina, that means you arrived about -- in Vitina at around the 7th of May -- I mean the 5th of July. I got my numbers and dates mixed up. Yes, the 5th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we then agree that you arrived in Heliodrom sometime in November 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The end of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, in the statement you say that in the village of Vrde you spent 105 days in that village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, when we add all those days up, it would appear that you spent about a month in Vitina in actual fact? If you do the maths perhaps you can arrive at that same conclusion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there for about two months.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, this village, Vrde, is a village between Mostar and Jablanica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far the village is from Vitina, roughly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't look to see. There was a tarpaulin on the vehicle so I couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know how long you were driven from Vitina to Vrde?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in the village of Vrde, you never returned to Vitina, is that right, but you went from Vrde, where you were in November 1993, you were taken to Heliodrom. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that your - if I can use the term - stay in the village of Vrde, the time you spent in Vrde, was a separate event, separate from your stay in Vitina, regardless of the fact that they were linked by the very fact that you were in captivity. But they're two localities and you spent time there at separate times. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next counsel. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Cross-examination by Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic:

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I also have just a few questions for you. Tell me, please, in the same statement that you were provided with by my colleague you said that apart from the one event with Mr. Tabakovic, that incident, that throughout the time you spent in Vitina or Otok, the inmates were not physically maltreated, do you remember saying that; and if so, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you the following. Tell me, please, the aluminium hangar that was mentioned -- was it a hangar -- when you say "hangar," do you mean a building with walls and a roof? That's what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's built of aluminium, tin, a tin hangar with a roof, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And did it have walls too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, tin walls. It was all tin, the roof and the walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I know that this question might be strange and unusual, but I'm asking it and stating this for the benefit of Their Honours and the Trial Chamber. Witness E was heard in this same courtroom, and on pages of the transcript from 22068 to page 22071, in describing the conditions in Otok, this witness said that there was no firm building there, that there was just a shelter, a roof shelter without any walls. That's why I ask this witness that question. That same witness whom I've just mentioned, sir, told us - and you can see this from his statements, also with reference to those pages in the transcript - that Otok -- that security was provided at Otok exclusively by the home guard and that the military police, even in those first days would stop by there from time to time, either when asked to come or to effect control. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask -- my next question will be my last question, my last topic, rather. Now, we saw the Red Cross certificate a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember who issued you with that certificate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you receive it from someone from the Red Cross or from some other person? You don't need to know their name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you read what it says on the certificate when you received it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And before you arrived here in the courtroom, did you ever tell anybody that this date, the 2nd of January, recorded on the certificate was wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not what I have. This is what I was given.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But did you say that -- did you tell anybody that before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Who did you draw attention to this mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this man here. I said there was a mistake on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you tell the Prosecutor in preparing to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I told him. I said this was not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But before that you told no one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told no one before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We just have one document. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Could the usher come up and get it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And while we're distributing the document, it's just a list with names and it will be distributed to everyone including the Prosecutor. You told the Prosecutor that from the 2nd of August, 1992, you were a resident of a place called Novi Seher; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, let's look at this document together, it's P 09440, it is a Prosecution document. Unfortunately, I don't know the date because it was accessed electronically and we couldn't find a date anywhere. Anyway, it is a list of detained citizens from Novi Seher held in Otok camp, Vitina. I don't even know who the author of the document is, it doesn't say. But anyway, sir, would you now look at the name under number 160 and tell me whether you recognise that name. I'm not going to say it out loud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You know who it's about and who the man is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And we mentioned him today, did we not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, we just have enough time for you to look through this list of names and tell me if you recognise anybody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, I've taken a look at the list, too, but nowhere on this list did I see your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Have you had a look at the list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name wasn't there. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That completes my cross-examination. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just two brief areas to cover and with a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I just have a few questions for you. Today here you mentioned - and that was on page 91 of the transcript - when you were asked about when you were at Gola Brda, you mentioned a man from Dubrovnik and allegedly someone from the HV. Now I'm going to ask you the following, this man from Dubrovnik, the person who said he was from Dubrovnik, did he have HVO insignia on his uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We didn't dare look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you talked to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, while we were working, that's what he told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You heard him speak but you didn't see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you didn't see any insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, in the way he spoke, did he speak the dialect of people from Bosnia-Herzegovina, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't say. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, the tank, did you see a tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you see any inscriptions on the tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You didn't?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we weren't close enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right. So you don't know what markings the tank had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And now to move on to another area. You also spoke about the fact that you worked up at that position by the relay station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When you returned back from the relay station or -- well, you said you went there and that you were a human shield up there. Just three brief questions. Up at those positions while there was fighting going on there, did you ever hear that the HVO had any dead on its side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Anything more precise? Did you hear how many casualties, fatalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, two on both sides, both on the HVO side and the BH army side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Not more than that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Did the HVO have any wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one, and I carried him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You don't know whether there were more than one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And this human shield that you mentioned, in that human shield none of you were killed, right, there were no fatalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And none of you were wounded either, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next counsel, if any? No. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No questions. We just wish to thank the gentleman for coming here to give his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ibrisimovic, no questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Nozica, you're hidden from me there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. On behalf of my colleagues, I thank you for coming to testify in The Hague, and I wish you a safe journey back home in your country, but please don't move because we need to remove the screen behind you before rising. Next week, Mr. Scott, what's the programme?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I would like to address -- I don't want to impose on the Court's generosity in saying that we might a have few extra -- a couple of extra minutes, but I would like to address both next week and a couple of other outstanding matters, Your Honours, if I could have about four minutes of the Chamber's time, but I think it would be best if the witness was excused, if we could have the witness excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we are going to lower the blinds so that the witness can leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of January, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: [The accused Petkovic and Pusic not present]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.03 p.m.,
